result.summary:
The magazine-fit design was already finished in 395afe83. The scripts were last edited at 01:14, and the stage-2 run at 01:23 used that code, so there was nothing left to build. The real-pattern geometry is in place: a front trunnion block (X >= 418, under Z -5) holding the chamber mouth and feed ramp, and a front-lug pocket with a ledge where the hook tab seats; its roof is the front top stop. The well opening is the swept envelope of the magazine plus clearance, and the catch nose is an arc about its pin, sitting under the rear lug. The rock is 8 deg about M (426.7, -28.0), then an 8 mm insert. I checked the magfit renders (cut section, trunnion from below, seam) and the grey renders: the seam is tight and even, and the outside shape is unchanged.

Clean rebuild: run_rifle.sh passed every gate (blockout plus all form gates, B3/B4/G5 and MAGFIT M1-M5). The first full run_game.sh ended with 2 new failures, both fixed:
1) LOD2 rifle share was 18.1% against an 18% limit. The trunnion cuts added triangles at LOD2. At LOD2 only (6.7 m and beyond) the receiver now leaves out the feed ramp and uses one merged lug/tab pocket. Both are inside the trunnion and can't be seen. Receiver LOD2 went from 698 to 562 triangles, so the share is now 17.8%. LOD0 is byte-identical.
2) One mirrored UV triangle on the new magazine: a 29 x 0.43 mm sliver on a rib flank. In the curved-magazine side chart a long chord bows enough to flip a face that thin. The fix is in the shared library (gunlib/uvchart.py, _unflip_polar_caps): such faces now use the frame's flat chart, which can never mirror. All other UVs are unchanged.
The second full run_game.sh passed stage 3 (22/22 gates) and stage 4 (23/23).

No export or rig was done. Note that Exports/Guns/AR01/Textures was regenerated by the paint step, so it no longer matches the SK/SM FBXs still shipped from 642606d2. The next stage's re-export brings them back in line.
issues: Look issue already in the previous build (not caused by this stage): a bright bare-metal wedge, about 5 mm, on the magazine's flat side next to a rib (face around (145, +-13, -28) in the grip frame; visible in review/tex/cu_mag_left.png). The baked edge mask reads high there (e1 ~0.12, e2 ~0.24), so the paint step chips it. The same face had 14% bright texels in the 642606d2 build. No gate catches it; it is worth raising with the realism judges or in the next look pass.
The paint step's 'spread' blur (rifle_paint.py) is normalised over every valid texel, not per island, so edge wear can leak across a close island border. It is minor and was not changed.

The visible gap at the front of the well where the lug channel sits is 1.97 mm when seen from below. That is the real pattern's lug slot; it is reported separately in F2 and is outside the 0.8 mm seam target for that small width.
G5-visible at LOD3 reads FAIL (max 6.25 px). It is info only in game.json and unchanged from before.
The Exports textures now match the new UVs while the exported SK_AR01/SM_AR01 FBXs still carry the old UVs and magazine. The next stage (run_rig_mag.sh) must re-export before Unreal checks.

result.summary:
I fixed the texture problems the realism judges found, re-ran every stage-3 gate on the final maps, and rendered review/realism_tex2 (fp_35cm, ads_55deg, tp_3m, hero_34, plus contact.png, ads_55deg_notch.png and ads_check.json). Stages 3 and 4 both pass. Nothing was exported.

Wood: the grain now follows each part's shape. A new helper in gunlib/paint.py lays the grain along each piece. The lines run with the stock's drop and narrow through the wrist, and lean with the grip. The butt, grip toe and guard ends show end grain: darker, rougher, with ring arcs. Ring widths are irregular, and each part now has colour variation inside it (darker streaks and patches, golden lighter areas, fine pores) and uneven sheen. Each part's median colour is held in place, and the per-part tones were re-calibrated over 5 rounds. L5 passes on every region (stock R/B -0.068). The one-stain + per-part tone design is kept, and the recolour pre-check passes.

Dust cover: the whitish patches and long scuff streaks are gone. It is now one dark coat with a faint mottle (crown BC p50 71, p99 84). Wear sits on the edges, the rear lip and around the button. The cover's UVs are not stretched (anisotropy p50 1.007, p95 1.24) and its density is 114.5 px/cm (class A). L5 dust_cover passes (luma -0.026).

Bright patches: the gas-block collar patch and the ring at the brake base came from the wear band spreading up to about 2 mm off edges. Bare steel now only appears right on sharp edges, broken into irregular flecks, and worn steel is rougher (0.50-0.62) so it reads mid grey. The largest bare blob is now 5.9 mm2.

ADS: the post was always there. At 1600 px it was about 4 px wide, too small to spot. The render now uses the exact B4 camera at the gate's own 2560x1440. The post shows 8x20 px with its tip within 0.5 px of the B4 point, at a contrast of -0.44 against the notch opening.

I added 3 new gates to uv_bake_paint.json: wear blobs, cover crown, and the ADS check.
issues: Furniture median colour is fixed by L5 to the sheet's saturated orange-red walnut (stock R/B about 2.5), so the overall hue stays orange; only the variation inside each part changed.

Recolour default path vs the shipped BC now differs by more (per-part levels p99.9 28-49): the hue variation inside each part lives only in the BC. This is an informative number, not a gate. Stage 9 still needs Use Original Baked Colours ON.
At first-person distance a faint lighter halo is still visible around the cover's button hole, and there are a few sparse bright chips on the rear trunnion and receiver straight edges.
The dust cover crown still reads mid grey in the ADS view because a dark coat seen at a glancing angle reflects the grey environment; the texture itself is dark (sRGB 71).
Not mine, left as is: the existing stage-4 log shows the info line 'G5-visible LOD3 worst mean 2.279 max 6.250 px FAIL'. The stage-4 record passes because its G5 gates use penetration depth.
Blind tests and the two judges' re-review of realism_tex2 have not been run.

reasons: The silhouette and part layout read correctly as a stamped-receiver AK (slant brake, gas block, front sight, rivet pattern, trunnion, selector, sling loops). The finish is what gives it away as CG.

The wood is a flat, saturated orange-red with a glossy plastic sheen. The grain is long, even streaks, most visible on the stock comb and the lower handguard. There is no darker end grain, no oil soak, no grime in the corners and no dents or wear on the edges, so it reads like stained plastic, not old birch or beech.

The receiver, dust cover and barrel are all the same uniform mid-grey with the same matte response. Blued or parkerised steel would vary in tone, with a darker oily sheen on the dust cover and a polished bolt carrier. Here everything looks like one grey paint.

The edge wear is thin, bright white dashes and specks, on the magazine ribs, receiver edges and trunnion. They look like an edge mask with a white fill, not worn-through steel, which shows as soft, slightly shiny metal on corners and contact points. On the magazine they read as white scratch lines, not as wear on the paint.
The dust cover is plain and smooth with soft, rounded shading. A stamped AKM-type cover has transverse stiffening ribs, and the smooth cover makes the top line look like a blockout.
The pistol grip's checkered panel is a flat inset that is too sharply bounded and cleaner than the grip around it. It reads as a decal-like patch.
The magazine is the same flat dark grey as the receiver. A real steel mag has a different tone and finish from the receiver, or would be orange Bakelite, so there is no material separation.

At first-person distance the dust cover renders as a light, chalky grey that looks like primer or clay, not blued steel. Its top surface shows uneven, lumpy shading (soft waves and dents), as if the mesh or normals are not flat, which no stamped steel cover has.
The rear edge of the dust cover and the receiver's rear lip have rows of bright white dash marks. They read as a procedural edge-wear stripe, not real wear.
The dust cover has no ribs, so the large flat top that fills the screen in first person has no believable detail. This is the view players see most.
The stock and handguard are bright orange with almost no visible grain or wear at this distance. They look like a toy or a block of plastic.
The rear sight base and leaf are lit almost white, the same brightness as the dust cover. Machined sight parts would be darker blued steel.
The rear trunnion cap screw and the dark rear edge are fine. The metal colour and surface quality dominate the view and make it read as CG.

The dust cover fills the bottom half of the frame as a near-white, softly lumpy surface. It shows broad uneven shading bands and scattered dark specks, like plaster or primer, not dark oiled steel. In an aim-down-sights view this is the most visible surface in the game, and it immediately reads as wrong.
There are no stiffening ribs on the dust cover and no sheen along its length, so it looks like a smooth tube, not pressed sheet metal.

The rear sight block and leaf are light grey with bright white edge outlines. Real rear sights are dark blued steel, often blackened to cut glare. A light sight picture is visually and functionally wrong.
The charging handle knob reads as bright polished chrome with a toy-like specular highlight. It does not match the matte finish of the rest of the metal.
This is a diagnostic close-up of the sight picture. The notch and post alignment geometry is plausible, with a U notch, the post centred, and the protective ears on the front sight seen behind it.
Every edge of the leaf and the ears has a crisp, bright white rim, like an outline shader or edge-wear mask. Real sight edges are dark, sometimes with slight wear, but never outlined white.
The leaf face is a flat, even grey with no blued-steel depth, so it looks like a vector-flat CG surface.
The right panel's red post is a debug marker, not a realism issue, but it confirms this frame is a check render, not a shippable view.

At 3 m third-person distance the silhouette, proportions, magazine curve, slant brake, front sight and stock drop all read as a correct stamped-receiver AK pattern. A player would accept it at a glance.
Minor: the wood is still noticeably redder and more saturated than real furniture, and the metal is a single uniform grey. At this size that only looks slightly clean or new, not fake.
Minor: there is no visible material difference between the magazine and the receiver, which costs some realism even at range.

This is a composite of the four views. The two first-person/sights frames (top row) clearly fail: the dust cover looks chalky light grey with a lumpy, wavy surface, has no ribs, has white dashed edge wear, and the sight parts are lit near white.

The bottom-right hero frame has a correct silhouette, but the wood is glossy orange with stretched, even grain, the metal is a single flat grey, and the white scratch-line wear on the magazine and edges reads as CG.
Only the small 3 m frame (bottom-left) holds up, because the material faults are too small to see at that size.

The shape is right: a classic stamped receiver with rivets and the trunnion and dimple pattern, a slant brake, a 45-degree gas block, a cleaning rod, a ribbed curved mag and a checkered grip. The finish is what gives it away.

The magazine edge wear is drawn as thin bright white streaks running along every rib and edge, evenly spaced and the same brightness everywhere. It looks like painted-on edge highlights, not worn-through finish. Real mag wear is patchy, shows dull bare steel and sits on the high points and the feed lips.

The metal is one flat, even dark grey across the receiver, dust cover, barrel, gas tube and front sight. There is no blued or parkerized sheen, no difference between parts, no oil or dirt, and the receiver edges and rivets show almost no wear. It reads like a clay or untextured material.

The wood is saturated orange-red with an even plastic-looking gloss. The grain on the stock is broad, swirly and blurry, like a stretched procedural texture with no pores. The handguards are the same tone and grain as the stock, which looks like one material assigned everywhere.
The upper handguard shows a hard horizontal step or ledge partway down its side, with a pale line on it. It looks like a modelling or UV seam rather than real handguard shape.
The checkering on the grip is a dark printed patch on a smooth glossy surface. It does not catch light like cut wood.
The dust cover top is pale, washed-out light grey, much lighter than the receiver sides. It looks like primer or untextured clay, not blued or painted steel.
The dust cover surface looks lumpy and soft, with uneven low-frequency waves in the shading. A pressed sheet steel cover should read crisp and even, with sharp stamped ribs.
The rear of the dust cover and the receiver rear edge have small scattered white chalky specks and dashes. They read as decal noise or texture artefacts rather than worn finish.
The wood at the stock tang and handguard is bright orange and glossy with almost no visible grain at this distance, which looks like plastic.
There is a hard brightness jump between the light dust cover and the dark side rails. It makes the parts look like separately assigned materials, not one finished gun.
The dust cover fills the lower frame and renders almost white-grey, like matte plaster. A real firearm here shows dark steel with subtle specular sheen.
The dust cover surface has visible waviness and blotchy dark specks that look like noise stamped onto clay, not wear, pitting or oil.
The charging handle knob shows a bright, near-chrome highlight. It does not match the matte, almost unshaded receiver and looks like a different material.
The rear sight block and leaf geometry read correctly. The materials around them destroy the realism.
The sight picture is believable: the front post sits centred in the rear notch, with its top level with the leaf top, and the hood ears flank it. This matches a real AK-pattern sight picture.

This is a diagnostic crop (the right half has a red-tinted post), so it is not a natural view. One small note: a thin bright highlight runs around the whole leaf top and notch edge, plus a white fleck at the upper-left corner. It slightly suggests an outline shader, but a player would not call the sight fake from this.
At 3 m the silhouette and proportions read clearly as a real stamped-receiver rifle: the stock drop, grip angle, mag curve, handguard split, gas tube, front sight post and brake are all right.
At this range the wood tone darkens to a more believable walnut-brown and the flat metal does not stand out. A player would accept it at a glance.
Minor: the metal is uniformly flat and dark, with no specular variation between receiver and barrel.

This is a contact sheet of the four views. Both close views (first person and ADS) fail clearly because of the near-white, lumpy, clay-like dust cover and chalky white specks. The hero shot fails on the painted-looking white streak wear on the mag and the flat grey metal plus glossy orange wood.

Only the 3 m view passes. Overall the shape is credible but the final textures read as CG: the metal finish lacks a blued or parkerized look, the edge wear looks stylised, and the wood looks plastic and over-saturated.

result.summary:
I re-exported stage 5 and rebuilt and fitted stage 6 on the new trunnion geometry and maps using run_rig_mag.sh. Each step after the build ran in a fresh Blender process on the exported bytes. The final run passes every gate: rig_export.json is PASS (14 gates) and mag.json is PASS (M1-M8, C1, S1, qa, LODs, B10). The SK_AR01 set, the 5 clips, the physics proxy, SM_AR01 and SM_AR01_Mag are all re-shipped. The shipped rifle sha256 is 4c160d36...f1ff and the magazine was built from those bytes.

The first run had 4 failures, all caused by the scripts, not the geometry:
1) S1 failed at 0.005 mm against a 0.001 mm limit. game_report keeps the centre of mass rounded to 0.01 mm. The SK_AR01 sockets used that rounded value, but SM_AR01's sockets have the exact value. Fix in rifle_rig.py: the rig now takes the exact centre of mass from the stage-4 socket on SM_AR01_LOD0, the same way MagInsertStart is set exactly. It stops with an error if that value is more than 0.0051 mm from the report. rifle_rig_verify.py now records and checks that difference (0.0048 mm).
2) M3 failed: rear lug to catch was 0.626 mm. The fit gate's rear-lug window was left over from the old design (X >= 368) and missed the new lug's rear face at X ~367.3. I set the window to match the form gate (X 366-374, Z -40.5 to -34.5). It now measures 0.200 mm, the same as form gate F3.
3) and 4) M4 and M5 failed because, at LOD3 only, the magazine touches the catch by up to 0.59 mm during the insert. The catch exception was applied as if it were a LOD0 contact. The gate's own threshold says LOD2-3 pairs are judged in pixels at the switch distance. Those contacts are now judged that way: the worst is 0.10 px, against a 1 px limit. The LOD0 contacts still use the strict catch exception: the catch nose only, at a rock of 0.75-1.25 deg, at most 0.041 mm deep.

I checked the renders. The rock strip shows the hook tab going into the trunnion pocket and the rear lug passing under the catch. The rig contact sheet shows seated, rocked, insert start, dropping and bolt-back poses. One cosmetic issue: a rig render is still named reload_f09_rocked18 although the rock is now 8 deg. No background processes are left running. Nothing was committed.

result.summary:
All review renders are made from the exported files only. Two new scripts do the work. gunlib/export_review_job.py is a headless Blender job that the SMG can reuse. It imports SK_AR01.fbx and its LOD1-3 files, puts SM_AR01_Mag.fbx on the magazine bone (or at a socket), imports the A_AR01_Charge and A_AR01_ReloadEmpty clips, and builds materials from the shipped textures through gunlib.game.game_material (BC sRGB, ORM linear, N DirectX). rifle/rifle_review_export.py sets up the cameras and builds the pairs and contact sheets. The SHA-256 of every input file is recorded in gates/review_export.json.

(a) Blind test: 12 pairs, 24 images, in review/blind/. They cover both sides, the top, the 3/4 view, the close-ups c1-c7 and a seated mag/well crop at 6x. Ours is image B on pairs 1, 2, 4, 7, 8 and 11. The key is review/blind_key.json and an unblinded contact sheet is in review/blind_src/.
- Side and top cameras rebuild each trace panel's pixel-to-mm mapping, including the form gate's fit. The true-left camera looks from +Y, so its image matches the unmirrored RIGHT panel.
- The 3/4 view uses scratch/q34/camera.json. Each close-up uses its own panel camera. c1 poses the selector 13.25 deg, c4/c5 show the magazine alone, and c7 clips everything forward of the stock.
- Our silhouette IoUs reproduce the earlier gate numbers, so the framing matches.
- To keep resolution equal, ours is rendered at 3x, composited on the panel's own fitted backdrop, reduced to the panel's pixel size, then enlarged with the same LANCZOS filter as the reference. Side panels are cut above the ruler.
- Lighting: sides and top use the L5 physical rig (k 1.332 from l5.json), placed relative to each camera. I changed the top view to this so the overhead key no longer washes out the dust cover. The 3/4 view and close-ups use the detail kit's rough rig.

(b) Realism set (review/realism/): fp_35cm, ads_55deg (2560x1440), tp_3m and hero_34, with a contact sheet. Review set (review/set/, 19 images): receiver right/left at 3x; front sight and brake right/left/3-4; three magazine views at 2x; three reload views at MagRockStart; two bolt views at full rearward travel (101.2 mm); LOD strip and LOD wireframe strip; three wireframe views; tp_8m.

No Blender or Unreal processes were left running.
issues: Likely design tells for the blind judge (I looked; these come from the asset, not from how it was rendered): the steel looks flat mid-grey and clean where the sheet shows dark worn steel. The same look appears in the earlier build-blend texture renders (review/tex), so the import is faithful. BC median is 53 (#353535); ORM roughness is about 0.53, metallic 0. The wood is smooth and uniform where the sheet shows worn grain.

c7 butt plate: our plate fills the whole stock end, and the wood flanks the sheet shows around a narrower plate are almost missing. This is a design or close-up stylisation difference (spec R36: main views win). It is not caused by the camera clip.
c4 magazine close-up framing IoU is only 0.72, the same as its panel camera's own solve, so the matched framing of that pair is approximate.
With the bolt fully back, the open ejection port shows an almost black, empty interior. The realism judge may comment on it.
The '3x' and '2x' scales are my choice, since nothing specified them: 1x = 2560 px across the 880 mm gun (2.91 px/mm), so 3x = 8.73 px/mm and 2x = 5.82 px/mm.

reasons: Shape and proportions read correctly as a classic stamped-receiver rifle: slant brake, front sight block, 90-degree gas block, gas tube with vent holes, cleaning rod, rivets, trunnion, curved ribbed mag, and the selector and charging handle all sit in the right places. The fake read comes from the finish, not the form.

The metal is one flat, even mid-grey (like matte primer) on receiver, dust cover, barrel, gas tube and mag. Real blued or phosphated steel shifts between parts: barrel and gas tube look different from the stamped receiver, and edges and high points show subtle sheen and darkening. Here every part has the same albedo and roughness.

The wood is a saturated orange-cherry with stripy procedural grain and an even plastic sheen. It reads as a shader, not oiled or lacquered birch or beech. The grain does not follow the shape of the stock comb or the pistol grip.

The upper handguard shows a hard painted line and band running across it (looks like a texture seam or baked-in groove), plus a pale grain blotch that does not match the lower handguard. The two handguard pieces look like two different materials.
The grip checkering is a sharp-edged rectangular patch that reads like a decal stuck on flat wood. Real cut checkering on a curved grip sits in a borderline cut and wraps with the surface.

Mag wear is even white streaks running along every rib and edge: the classic look of an automatic edge-wear generator. Real wear clusters at the feed lips, the front lug, the floorplate edges and the spine contact points, and it shows bare dark-grey steel, not white.
The rubber or steel buttplate rim is a light-grey band with noisy speckle that does not read as a steel buttplate.
Overall a weapon artist would say 'clean CG asset with generator wear' at a glance, even though the silhouette passes.

In first person, the dust cover fills the frame as a pale, near-white, chalky surface. It reads as unpainted plastic or clay, not dark finished steel. Under the same lights, the receiver side reads much darker, so the top surface roughness and albedo look wrong.

The dust cover top looks lumpy and wavy, like soft dents or blotchy normal-map baking, not a crisp pressed sheet with clean stamped ribs. A real stamped cover has a taut surface with sharp formed edges.
White chip speckles bunch in a line along the rear edge of the dust cover and on the rear trunnion face. They read as procedural noise from a mask generator, not as real wear on contact edges.
The rear-sight leaf and slider are lit much brighter than the rest, so they read as bare aluminium.
The wood at the bottom of the frame is bright orange with a plastic highlight, which pulls the eye and looks toy-like next to the grey metal.
The close-up exposes how little the materials vary: no oil sheen, no finish wear on the dust-cover button or the charging-handle path, no micro-roughness breakup.

The sight picture is broken. Looking through the rear-sight notch, no front sight post is visible; the notch shows only background. Any player would call this wrong at once, because an ADS view of this pattern must show the front post centred in the rear notch.
The dust cover takes up most of the frame as a very light, matte, putty-grey surface with soft lumps and dents, and it reads like a clay render. It does not look like dark finished stamped steel.
The rear-sight base and leaf look clean and plausible as geometry, but the material matches the clay-like cover, with no finish change or edge wear on the sliding parts.
The charging-handle knob at the right edge is a smooth, glossy, rounded blob with a different finish from everything else, so it reads as CG.
The sparse dark speckle dots scattered across the cover look like noise-texture pitting, not a real worn finish.
At 3 m the silhouette, stock-to-receiver drop, mag curve, gas-block angle, front sight and slant brake all read correctly. A player would accept it at a glance.

Small nits that still show even at this size: the wood is a bit uniform and saturated, and the metal is flat mid-grey with no bluing contrast, so it looks slightly 'game-ready clean' rather than service-worn. Not enough to call it fake at this distance.
This is a composite of the four views above, and two of them fail: the ADS view shows no front post in the rear notch, and the first-person view shows a pale, lumpy, clay-like dust cover.
The hero tile shows the even grey metal, the orange shader-look wood, the decal-like grip checkering, and the generator-style white streak wear on the mag.
Only the 3 m tile passes. Up close the asset reads as CG, so it does not meet the bar for a realistic stamped-receiver rifle.

Reads immediately as a correct stamped-receiver AK-pattern rifle: proportions, slant brake, front sight block with ears, gas block, gas tube with vent holes, cleaning rod, curved ribbed steel mag, long stamped selector, trigger guard and rear trunnion rivets all sit where they should.

Not perfect though: the wood is too saturated orange and evenly glossy, more like varnished plastic than oiled or shellacked birch. The stock's grain is a large swirly procedural pattern that looks painted on, and the handguards are a slightly different tone with cleaner grain.

The metal finish is a flat, uniform mid-grey with almost no bluing or parkerising variation, no oil sheen, and very little believable edge wear on the receiver corners, trunnion, dust cover edge or muzzle. Players would see it as a clean CG material, not a used rifle.
The mag wear is light vertical streaks plus a few white specks. It reads as scratches added on top, not paint worn off the high spots of the ribs and lips.
The checkered wooden pistol grip looks fine, but the checkering is very fine and flat, like a normal-map print.
Overall it is a believable mid-quality game asset at a glance, and the shape is right. The tells are in the materials.
In first person the dust cover renders as a light, almost clay-grey, smooth soft-edged slab. It does not read as thin pressed blued steel: it is too light, too matte and too thick.

The dust cover top looks wavy and lumpy, as if a sculpt or normal map is wobbling it, instead of a crisp pressed sheet. A stamped AK dust cover is either uniformly smooth or has crisp stamped ribs, never soft undulations.

Bright white pixel specks are scattered along the rear edge of the dust cover, the receiver top lip and the rear trunnion. They look like texture or bake noise, not edge wear, which would follow the corners continuously.
The rear of the receiver and the dust cover release button area look blocky and low-detail at this distance, which is the most-seen view in an FPS.
The receiver and dust cover differ in value so much that the cover reads as a different material, like grey plastic on black metal.
The saturated orange wood on the handguard and stock wrist stands out against the grey and reads as candy-coloured.
The silhouette (rear sight leaf, front sight, mag) is correct, so this is a material/finish failure, not a shape failure.

The dust cover fills most of the frame as a pale grey, softly lit, lumpy surface with visible undulating dents and blotchy dark specks. It looks like an untextured clay sculpt, not blued or painted pressed steel.
There is no specular breakup, no machining or stamping marks, and no finish texture, so at this zoom it reads as CG immediately.

The rear sight block and leaf are plausible in shape, but the notch area looks plain and boxy. The front post is not clearly framed in the rear notch; mostly the front sight ears show above the leaf, so the sight picture does not read as a clean AK alignment.
The bright charging handle knob on the right is fine in shape, but it is shinier than any other metal, which is inconsistent.
The top cover edges have soft, rounded, bevelled transitions instead of the crisp, thin rolled edge of a stamped cover.

At 3 m the silhouette is a convincing, correctly proportioned AK-pattern rifle: stock drop, pistol grip angle, curved mag, receiver length, handguard, gas tube, front sight and brake all read correctly.
The wood is darker and less orange under this lighting and looks fine. The metal reads as dark blued steel.
The only minor tell is the uniform clean finish with no visible wear breakup. That does not matter at this distance.
This contact sheet combines all four views. The third-person and hero panels pass as a real AK-pattern rifle, but the first-person and ADS panels, the two views a player sees most, fail.
Across views the dust cover/receiver top changes from near-black (third person) to pale clay-grey (first person/ADS), so the metal material does not hold up close.
Shared material problems: oversaturated orange wood with procedural swirl grain, a uniform matte-grey metal finish, and speckle-noise 'wear' instead of believable edge and contact wear.

The shape is credible in every panel. The fixes needed are surface finish on the dust cover and receiver (darker blued/painted steel, crisp pressed surface without waviness, proper edge wear), plus toned-down wood colour and grain.

issues.area: Wear (G9/G15): magazine, receiver magwell, trigger guard plate, brake collar
issues.claim: Bare-steel wear shows up as fake geometric marks. There are hard-edged white TRIANGLES in the middle of flat panels, away from any edge or handling zone, and regular dashed or dotted white lines that follow UV seams or straight edges. The sheet shows soft grey rubbing on exposed edges and rib crests only. Evidence (display coords): review/set/mag_left_2x.png (630,585); mag_34_2x.png triangles on the feed-lip block (300-330,190-240), (390,690), (730,940); reload_magrockstart_right_3x.png (700-745,630-660), (870-910,1180-1210), (1500-1520,1470-1490); reload_magrockstart_34_below.png (510-540,480-500), plus a dashed white line down the magazine rear spine (scratchpad crop catch34.png); brake_front_sight_34_3x.png has a dashed white seam line round the brake collar (820-840,490-720). The straight, triangle-shaped edges point to the edge masks (on_edge / on_edge_mag in rifle_paint.py) picking up the long sliver triangles of the CDT-triangulated flats; see wireframe_receiver_3x.png.
issues.fix: Bake or recompute the edge-wear and bevel masks in texture space from the high-poly. Do not rasterise them per low-poly triangle, and mask out triangle edges that lie inside planar faces. Allow bare chips only where curvature > 0 within 0.6 mm of a real convex edge (plus the METAL_WEAR handling zones), and break the chip outlines with noise so no chip has more than 50 % straight boundary. Kill the seam-following stipple: dilate the masks across UV seams or move the seams into cavities. Add a gate that counts bare-texel clusters on panel interiors (more than 2 mm from any convex edge) outside wear zones: the count must be 0.

issues.claim: A bright wedge-shaped sliver runs diagonally from the magazine-guide dimple and rivet down to the receiver's bottom corner at the front of the magwell. It is about 0.6 mm wide at the top and tapers to 0. It shows in every right-side and 3/4 textured render: receiver_right_3x.png display (1130-1300,590-700) (scratchpad crop rr_magwell.png), reload_magrockstart_right_3x.png (820-1030,500-610), reload_magrockstart_34_below.png (590-740,340-385), bolt_rear_34_above.png (800-980,830-900). It is NOT in the untextured clay render review/rig/fire_f03_bolt_rear.png (scratchpad crop clay_magwell.png), so the cause is the baked normal map or masks, not the geometry. It lines up with a long triangle edge in wireframe_receiver_3x.png. Neither the sheet nor the real pattern has any line there.
issues.fix: In T_AR01_Metal_N, force texels on the receiver_right planar faces back to the face normal wherever the decoded normal is more than 1 deg off (check G4 on the baked map per planar face, not only on the geometry). Then fix the cage or ray distance for that region; the front-trunnion / lug-recess cut changed the low-poly triangulation, so the CDT probably now has a sliver there. Re-bake the masks on the same cage. Re-render receiver_right_3x and confirm the line is gone.

issues.area: Moving parts: bolt / ejection port at full travel (user decision: full travel in the real port)
issues.claim: The receiver is still an empty shell at full bolt travel. The spec builds the carrier as a 72 mm visible face only (rifle_spec bolt_carrier dims carrier_visible_X 378-450). After the 101.2 mm stroke that face sits behind the port, so the port shows a black void containing only the far wall and a rail line. Brightening the port crop (scratchpad bolt_rear_right_3x_lift.png) shows no bolt head, no carrier body or piston extension crossing the port, no magazine follower or top lips, and no chamber face. Evidence: review/set/bolt_rear_right_3x.png port (750-1415,380-480) and bolt_rear_34_above.png (560-1200,580-750). At rest the port shows only a flat, smeared, polished plate (receiver_right_3x.png 940-1410,385-475). On a real stamped-receiver rifle you see the bolt's right side with the extractor at rest, and the bolt face plus magazine top at full rear.
issues.fix: Model the carrier body to real length so its forward body and piston extension still span the port at full rear. Add the rotating bolt head with the extractor claw and its slot (visible at rest at the front of the port, and its face at the rear end at full travel). Make sure the magazine follower or lips and the trunnion's chamber and feed-ramp face are visible through the port from the 34-above camera. Put these interior parts in the Metal set at class B and give them cavity darkening, not black (BC at least 35 sRGB). Re-render bolt_rear_* with the L5 rig plus a weak fill to prove it.

issues.area: Clips: selector state during Fire / Charge / ReloadEmpty
issues.claim: The Fire clip runs, and the bolt reaches full rear, with the selector on SAFE (lever up). Evidence: review/rig/fire_f03_bolt_rear.png, review/set/bolt_rear_right_3x.png. On the real pattern the safety lever in its top position blocks the trigger and stops the carrier's rearward travel, so firing or racking to full travel on SAFE is mechanically impossible and a known realism tell. The Selector clip itself is right: Safe -> Auto -> Semi order, 0-32 deg (rig_export.json notifies).
issues.fix: Remove the selector track from A_AR01_Fire, A_AR01_Charge, A_AR01_Reload and A_AR01_ReloadEmpty, so the game's AnimBP holds the selector state through a per-bone layered blend from the A_AR01_Selector poses, and document that in README/MATERIALS. Alternatively, key the selector at AUTO (16 deg) or SEMI (32 deg) for the whole length of those clips; first/last frames stay equal so looping is unaffected. Keep the static SM_AR01 rest pose on SAFE as the sheet shows it. Re-shoot the bolt-rear review frames with the lever down.

issues.claim: The catch reads as a melted chrome lump: a T/Y-section wedge with smooth-shaded, bent-normal faces and a mirror finish. Evidence: review/set/reload_magrockstart_34_below.png (330-410,660-790) (scratchpad crop catch34.png); receiver_right_3x.png display (815-890,840-935). On the sheet (both main side views) and on the real stamped rifle the catch is a flat stamped-steel paddle: a narrow flat tongue hanging behind the magazine, crisp bent edges, matte blued finish.
issues.fix: Rebuild it as about 1.5 mm stamped sheet: a flat tongue (about 8-9 mm wide) bent from the pivot plate, 0.2-0.3 mm crisp bevels, auto-smooth at 30 deg so the faces shade flat, and no rib. Use bluing roughness 0.45-0.55, with bare steel only on the tongue's lower edge where the thumb or magazine hits it. Re-check the B3 sweep 0-10 deg.

issues.claim: The upper handguard has baked line artifacts printed on it: a vertical line straight across the middle, with the grain changing across it, and a trapezoid outline matching the gas tube / handguard-liner shape that bleeds through the wood. issues.area: Review package lighting (G7/G20 evidence for the realism judges)
issues.claim: The close-up set and the FP / ADS / hero realism renders use the 'rough' rig (env 0.55, k 1.35, lights at 1.1 m), not the L5 physical rig (world 0.2) that the colour was calibrated on. Under this rig the black lacquer reads as grey paint or plastic and the wood as orange varnished pine. Measured value/background ratios: receiver flank 0.88 in receiver_right_3x and 0.69 in hero_34, against 0.53 on the sheet; lower handguard 0.99 against 0.67. The flank tone spread (p10-p90) is 80-88 against the sheet's 36-79. issues.claim: The rivet heads show about 8 visible facets in the textured exported LOD0. Evidence: receiver_right_3x.png rivets at display (780,430), (905,430), (930,575), (390,580), (95,600) in crop rr_port.png, and every rivet in rr_magwell.png; receiver_left_3x.png; bolt_rear_34_above.png. G3 requires a facet angle of at most 7.5 deg on rounds at LOD0, and these are clearly polygonal at 3x and at 35 cm first-person (about 16 px across).

issues.area: Small-part finish (G7): charging handle, selector, carrier flank
issues.claim: The small parts are polished to mirror chrome. The charging-handle knob is 79 % bare steel (look_polish.json) and reads as a chrome ball. The selector face flashes pure white in reload_magrockstart_34_below.png (0-270,250-400). The carrier flank in the port at rest shows cloudy smeared highlights (receiver_right_3x.png 940-1410,385-475), and the port throws a white glint at 3 m (tp_3m.png 750-800,440-450). The sheet shows all of these parts dark.

issues.claim: Uniform horizontal hairline streaks cover the whole receiver side and the front sight tower, like brushed aluminium. issues.claim: Small round pock dents are spread evenly over the handguards and grip, giving a hammered look under a clean even varnish. issues.claim: The window in the front sight tower is modelled as a near-rectangle with a slight slant (brake_front_sight_right_3x.png 545-660,350-435). issues.claim: On LOD3 the grip checkering renders as large black triangles, and on LOD2 the stock shades as visible faceted planes (lod_strip.png LOD3 grip at orig ~460-510,2290-2380; LOD2 stock 70-250,1500-1650). These could cause visible pops at the LOD switch.

issues.claim: The lever is modelled with a through slot. The sheet appears to show a recessed or fluted centre, and the real lever is solid with a recessed face.

issues.claim: Checked and acceptable against the sheet and the real pattern: the ADS sight picture (front post centred in the rear notch, ads_55deg.png, crop ads_notch.png); selector order Safe -> Auto -> Semi and its 0-32 deg arc; trigger and guard shape; modelled grip checkering panel; the rear-sight leaf's edge teeth and slider buttons (the sheet shows teeth); the slant brake with its side port (the sheet shows the port); magazine rib count, top block, front lug and floorplate button hole; the dust-cover button; the sheet-metal wall thickness visible at the port and the front-sight window; handed features (selector, port, charging handle) only on the true right; no markings.

result.verdict: L6 FAIL: 8 major issues against the "0 major" bar. The silhouette and proportion work holds, and most small parts follow the real pattern (sight picture, selector arc and order, trigger and guard, checkering, brake, leaf, magazine form). What fails is how the gun is surfaced and how it moves. (1) Wear is fake: triangle chips and dashed seam lines. (2) A baked diagonal sliver on the right receiver at the magwell; it is absent in clay, so it is a normal/mask bake error. (3) The receiver is still empty at full bolt travel: no bolt head, no carrier body, no follower or chamber seen through the port, which breaks the "full travel in the real port" decision. (4) The Fire, Charge and Reload clips run with the selector on SAFE, which is mechanically impossible. (5) The magazine catch is a blobby chrome lump instead of a stamped paddle. (6) The upper handguard carries baked gas-tube outline and seam lines. (7) The review set and realism frames were lit with the near 'rough' rig (receiver/background 0.88 vs the sheet's 0.53), so the judges would see grey-plastic metal and orange wood; the shipped maps are unchanged and L5-calibrated. (8) The rivets are visibly faceted (G3). Fix order: re-bake masks and normals (items 1, 2, 6), rebuild the carrier, bolt and catch (3, 5), correct the clip selector state (4), increase rivet segments (8), then re-render the set on the L5 physical rig (7) and re-run L6/L7. The exported bytes are technically sound, with one major look defect. I checked them myself in fresh headless Blender processes: a raw FBX parse with no importer, a Blender re-import, and my own fit and clip maths. All checks ran on the current Exports/Guns/AR01, whose sha256 hashes match rig_export.json, mag.json and review_export.json.

What passed:
- **qa_check:** SM_AR01 (budget 57,000, UV1 required) passes 92/92 and SM_AR01_Mag passes 80/80.
- **qa_skeletal (max_influences=1):** passes on all four SK LODs once the importer's 0.01 armature scale is applied. In the file itself the root is at scale 1 in cm.
- **Skeleton (raw FBX):** a root Null plus 8 LimbNodes with the spec's parents. Rest rotation is 0 and there is no PreRotation. Bone heads are within 0.0045 mm of the spec. Every vertex has exactly one weight of 1.0, and the magazine bone carries 0 vertices.
- **Clips (raw curves):** every clip starts and ends at rest. The bolt makes its full 103.25 mm in Fire, Charge and ReloadEmpty. Selector steps are 0/16/32 degrees. The notify frames line up with the motion (ChargeRear 12, BoltRelease 18, MagIn 53, selector frames).
- **Clips, posed on LOD0 at every key:** no bounds excursion, no moving part intersects the rest, and the magazine on its bone never intersects the rifle in Reload or ReloadEmpty. The catch deflects to -3 then -6 degrees at keys 51-52.
- **Sockets:** all 17 match the spec in name, bone, position (within 0.0034 mm) and rotation, in both the skeletal and static sidecars. The 5 magazine sockets match too; only CenterOfMass and Holster differ, because the build computes them.
- **Hulls:** 7 rifle and 2 magazine hulls, named UCX_<node>_NN, each with 27 vertices or fewer. Every LOD0 vertex lies inside a hull.
- **UVs:** the skeletal mesh stays in 0..1. The static twin's slots sit in their own U tiles (Metal 0..1, Furniture 1..2, Mag -1..0). LOD0 has no overlaps and no flipped triangles in any set.
- **Textures:** all square powers of two. BC and ORM are 8-bit; normal maps are 16-bit, DirectX convention (paint.py flips green).
- **Static twin:** its LOD0 equals SK LOD0 plus the shipped magazine to within 0.0001 mm.
- **Magazine fit, my own measurements:**
  - M1: 0 intersections at LOD0 and LOD1; LOD2-3 are shallow at the switch distance.
  - M2: top stop 0.296 mm. The receiver bottom sheet (Z_M -30.0 to -30.8) leaves 0.28-0.54 mm per side, front 0.29, rear about 0.4.
  - M3: front lug 0.27 mm, rear lug to catch 0.20 mm.
  - M4/M5: over 50 path poses, the only contact is the catch, at most 0.04 mm deep at 0.75-1.25 degrees. The clip deflects the catch at that point.
  - M8: a straight insert collides between 2 and 16 mm of travel, so the rock is needed.
- **Names and housekeeping:** both deny lists are clean over 692 names, file names and sidecar text. Every gun script derives ROOT from its own location. No stray processes: no Blender or Unreal is running, and the only related processes are other sessions' mcp-for-blender servers, which I left alone.

The major defect is bare-steel wear painted as whole flat triangles on the magazine, plus pale wedges on the receiver near the magazine well and on the handguard. Both are visible in the review renders taken from the exported bytes. There are also several minor issues: the static twin's magazine LODs, a budget gate whose wording doesn't match its check, the checkering method needing a ruling, the clip node defaults, and some document drift. One process note: I measured the receiver sheet's lateral seam on a grid and found it fine. A first section probe had suggested 6 mm slots, but that was the receiver interior above the sheet.

issues.area: Textures / look (Mag set, also seen on the receiver and handguard)
issues.claim: Bare-steel wear is painted as whole flat triangles, which show as white triangular shards in the review renders from the exported bytes (review/set/mag_34_2x.png, mag_left_2x.png, reload_magrockstart_34_below.png, receiver_right_3x.png). I sampled T_AR01_Mag_BC/ORM over each triangle of the shipped SM_AR01_Mag_LOD0. 476 triangles (122 mm2) are 100% bare steel (BC about 192, metallic 255), the largest single one is 25.9 mm2 (e.g. mag-local (50.9, ±14.5, -123.8)), and 837 triangles (601 mm2) are more than half bare. The largest connected bare-steel area in the Mag ORM is about 75 mm2, against the rifle's own limit of 8 mm2 per chip. The 'realism-tex: no blown wear masks' gate in uv_bake_paint.json only measured the rifle's lacquered parts (it reports gas_block, 5.9 mm2). The magazine's lacquer was never gated, even though it is seen up close in first person and during reloads. Grey triangular chips are also visible on the handguard in the 3/4-below render.
issues.fix: Extend the chip-size gate to the Mag set and to wood (largest chip at most 8 mm2, no triangle 100% bare unless it is under 1 mm2). Build the wear mask in texel space from a continuous edge or curvature bake (high-poly or AO-derived) with texel-scale noise, not as a whole-face value. Then repaint the Mag maps (paint step plus the mag stage), re-run the realism set and look at mag_34, mag_left and reload_34_below again.

issues.area: Look / receiver at the magazine well (R51 cut)
issues.claim: receiver_right_3x.png shows a bright, sharp-edged wedge on the lower front of the receiver's right side next to the well, and reload_magrockstart_34_below.png shows a pale diagonal line across the right side from a rivet to the well. The BC map does not explain them: only 6 outer-skin triangles there are light, totalling about 5 mm2. They are probably the new R51 cut-back faces, or a lit sliver where the cut sheet meets the trunnion.
issues.fix: Render the right side of the well area in close-up with flat shading and with the BC alone. If it is geometry, add a bevel or close the sliver gap; if it is shading, check that face's normals and normal-map bake. Then re-run the review renders.

issues.claim: The twin's merged magazine is not the shipped magazine below LOD0. Per LOD, the twin's magazine has 6666 / 6666 / 4430 / 108 triangles, while SM_AR01_Mag has 6666 / 1998 / 648 / 248. Twin LOD1 is therefore 28,442 triangles (53.8 % of LOD0, target about 45 %) and LOD2 is 12,638 (23.9 %, target about 15 %). The LOD2 magazine is up to 2.6 mm from the shipped LOD2, and the shipped LOD3 is up to 18.1 mm from the twin's 108-triangle LOD3 magazine. LOD0 matches exactly. The twin is the battle-royale loot mesh, so the extra triangles at LOD1-2 add up across instances.
issues.fix: Build each twin LOD from SK LOD n plus SM_AR01_Mag LOD n, either by moving the twin export after stage 6 or by calling the same magazine generator levels in rifle_game.py. Add a gate requiring the twin's magazine at each LOD to equal SM_AR01_Mag LOD n.

issues.claim: game.json passes 'LOD3 rifle tris' with the threshold text '1500-2500 (ceiling 2500)' at 1076 triangles, below the spec floor (budgets_triangles.rifle.lod3 = [1500, 2500]), so the check only enforces the ceiling. Also, rifle LOD0 is 46,204 triangles, above the 30-45k target but under the 50k ceiling.
issues.fix: Either enforce the floor or record a dated ruling in the spec that 1076 is acceptable (LOD-pop passes, max 1.41 px). Report the LOD0 overshoot against the target in the gate.

issues.claim: In the exported SK LOD0, the checkered grip panel is flat geometry: 74 triangles per side, about 613 mm2, face normals with |ny| of 0.98. The checkering exists only in T_AR01_Furniture_N, which tilts those triangles 30-50 degrees. RIFLE_BUILD_PLAN line 219 says 'checkering in the normal map', but the binding user decision says 'real modelled cuts baked to a crisp normal on lower LODs'. Read literally, that means cut geometry on LOD0 and the normal map only on LOD1 and below.
issues.fix: Get a ruling from the user. If LOD0 needs real cuts, generate the cut panel as LOD0 geometry and keep the baked normal for LOD1-3, making sure LOD0's own normal map is flat on that panel so the relief isn't doubled. Otherwise record that the decision means a normal map baked from modelled cuts on every LOD.

issues.claim: In each A_*.fbx, the bone nodes' default transforms are the clip's frame-1 pose, not the bind pose: Fire trigger at 12 degrees, Charge bolt at -2.032 mm, Reload and ReloadEmpty catch at -2.593 degrees, Selector at 2.5 degrees. Unreal samples the keyed curves, which are correct and rest at the first and last key, so the game is unaffected. Blender treats those defaults as the rest pose, though, so a buyer or a check that re-imports a clip in Blender sees offset motion; my first readback was shifted by exactly these amounts.
issues.fix: In Scripts/pipeline/skeletal_prop.export_skeletal_set, set the scene frame to the clip's first frame (or reset the pose to rest) before each animation export. This is a shared pipeline module, so check whether another chat owns it before editing.

issues.claim: The ShellEject notify is at frame 2 (0.033 s), but the bolt first moves at frame 3 (-70 mm) and reaches full rear travel at frame 4. A case is ejected once the bolt has pulled it past the port, so the shell would spawn before the carrier moves.
issues.fix: Move ShellEject to frame 3, or to frame 4 at full rear travel, in the sidecar notifies and in the Unreal harness (U9).

issues.claim: The shipped SM_AR01_Mag_LOD0 measures 26.0-26.6 mm thick at the top and at -20 mm, but 27.5-27.9 mm at the rib heights (-40, -90, -120 mm) and 29.0 mm overall (floor plate). R32 set 26.0 including the pressed ribs' depth, and the spec key dimension is 26.0. The ribs therefore appear pressed outward by about 1 mm a side. The fit is unaffected: the ribbed part never passes through the sheet opening.
issues.fix: Confirm whether the ribs are pressed outward (as on real magazines) and record the overall thickness at the ribs and floor plate in the spec. If R32 meant 26 as the outer maximum, press the ribs inward instead and re-run the L2 3/4 exception.

issues.claim: Exports/Guns/AR01 has no README.md or MATERIALS_README.md, although CLAUDE.md's layout requires them. game.json's mass note also refers to a README for the 3.1 kg physics mass.
issues.fix: Write both before the Unreal import and Fab stages: import settings, colour spaces, TEXTUREGROUP_Weapon/WeaponNormalMap, LOD screen sizes, socket recreation, FP/TP components with ForcedLodModel, the physics mass, and the material instance chain.

issues.claim: All 12 exported FBX files embed the absolute source path, including the Windows username and this worktree's path (C:\Users\Cody\Desktop\Blender_Projects\.claude\worktrees\gun-assets-creation-261bad\Assets\Guns\AR01.blend). Exports/Katana and Exports/Fan do the same, so this comes from the pipeline, not this asset.
issues.fix: For Fab builds, have the owner of Scripts/pipeline/export_fbx.py clear the SceneInfo document and source URLs, or post-process the FBX, under the pipeline owner's lock.

issues.claim: Twin LOD1 has 944 triangles whose three UVs sit on one point (4,929 mm2 in all, largest 354 mm2; e.g. receiver inner wall at (142.8,-19.7,75.1) and handguard interior) and 162 flipped UV triangles (304 mm2, largest 32.6 mm2). They are mostly hidden faces, and LOD0 has none. However, 'no mirrored islands' is only gated at LOD0, and inner faces that show through the ejection port during Charge would sample a single texel.
issues.fix: Add a LOD1-3 gate that counts flipped and point-mapped triangles by visibility (none on visible faces), and confirm the port-visible carrier and receiver interior keep real UVs at LOD1.

issues.claim: The spec and plan section 5.3 say Metal 2048 ('DECIDED R29'), Mag 2048 and Detail16 2048. The shipped maps are Metal 4096 (allowed by the user's rule), Mag 1024 (smallest power of two that holds class C) and Detail16 1024. Measured densities are class A medians of 104-115 px/cm and class B of 91.9 px/cm: above the 80-100 and 60-80 bands but within the +25 % tolerance. look_polish.json (10-05) is stale; uv_bake_paint.json carries the current L5 result.
issues.fix: Update rifle_spec.json textures.sets and plan section 5.3 to the shipped sizes with a dated note, and mark look_polish.json as superseded.

issues.claim: SK_AR01_LOD2 and SM_AR01_LOD2 reach Y +25.0 mm on the left side, against 22.22 at LOD0 (2.8 mm wider). LOD-pop still passes (max 1.80 px).
issues.fix: Find the LOD2 part that sticks out (probably a generator radius or segment fallback) and clamp it to the LOD0 envelope.
